,"eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a054a5-63a8-74c8-a1ee-b9a770d5e8de\u0022,\u0022ProjectId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:\u0022\\u0022The build session ends with an adversarial self-review phase: after all work is done and the suite is green, and before the recompose, the session re-reads its complete branch diff assuming it wrote defective code somewhere and its job is now to find it - hunting refactors, blast-radius gaps at sibling sites, and instructions it authored but never executed - fixing and checkpoint-committing what it finds, so the first external review pass starts from code that survived its own author\\u0027s hunt\\u0022\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022The dispatch prompt gains a named self-review phase in the end-of-work protocol, ordered after the full suite is green and before the recompose, and states the reason for that placement (the hunt must see finished work, and the recompose must compose the post-hunt tree)\u0022,\u0022The phase is framed adversarially in the prompt\\u0027s own words - the session is told to assume the branch contains defects it wrote and that its job has changed from author to hunter - and the framing is a stance switch on the finished diff, not a checklist recital\u0022,\u0022The hunt starts from a fresh git diff against the branch base read in full, not from the session\\u0027s memory of what it wrote\u0022,\u0022The prompt names three mandatory hunts - a refactor once-over of everything written; a blast-radius sweep where every changed behavior gets its sibling sites with the same shape enumerated and checked; and execute-your-own-instructions, where any skill step, command sequence, or documented procedure the session authored is actually run rather than proofread\u0022,\u0022Findings are fixed and checkpoint-committed before the recompose begins, and the prompt forbids deferring a self-review finding to a note or a comment - the phase ends with the defect fixed or a stated, checkable reason it is not a defect\u0022,\u0022Fix-round and follow-up prompts are unchanged - the phase belongs to the initial build session only\u0022,\u0022The build session\\u0027s model is unchanged, so before-and-after review-cycle counts attribute to the prompt alone\u0022,\u0022The existing end-of-work contract is preserved intact - checkpoint discipline, the gated recompose sequence, and the clean-tree final contract all still hold with the new phase inserted, and the prompt tests pin the phase\\u0027s presence and its ordering\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022## Background\\n\\nDiagnosed live on 2026-08-30 while shepherding cea5ae6e (nine review cycles) and b6dfcbe5 (conformance cap park). The review loop\\u0027s per-pass economics make every defect that survives the build expensive: a missed medium costs a full fix, verify, and fresh-full-pass lap, with two large-context review lenses per full pass. Two failure classes observed that day are within reach of the session that wrote the code, if it turned on itself before declaring done:\\n\\n1. **Incomplete application of a change.** Twice in one afternoon a session applied half of an explicitly multi-site fix (cea5ae6e cycle 6: the reflog fix landed in one of two branch-creating arms; b6dfcbe5\\u0027s park: a two-escape cancellation finding had one escape closed). A blast-radius sweep by the author would have enumerated the sibling sites.\\n2. **Authored instructions that were never run.** The commit-plan skill\\u0027s stash sequence was not executable as written; a reviewer found it by running it.
